title: Not what it’s cracked up to be.
text:
Not what it’s cracked up to be.. I’ve owned a Bunn coffeemaker for years that was on its last leg. I decided to venture out and try something different and after watching YouTube reviews for 4 hours and reading reviews, I decided to take the plunge and buy this maker as it had the highest rated in the price range I was looking at I love my coffee and am by far not a coffee “connoisseur”. I just love a good strong cup of coffee to get my day going. I’m a Foldgers kind of gal occasionally who occasionally steps into the wild side and buys Starbucks coffee (already ground) and maybe some flavored coffee here and there.
So let’s get to the “beans” of this. The maker itself is flimsy. As most pots do, it “sticks” to the counter as you pull it out to fill the water. The first time I pulled it out, I pulled the whole top section off the machine. Yes, heart attack ensued thinking I broke it. After wrestling with it and getting it back together, I push a washcloth under it for easier gliding. One would think for that amount of $$ it wouldn’t come apart quite so easy and wouldn’t be plastic. You’re unable to put the top of the carafe on while the filter is still in place. It’s not a huge thing, but beware of steam burns when you’re dumping the hot grounds.
Next, when you dump the water from the thermos carafe into the maker, be prepared to have water all over your counter. As there isn’t a pour spout in the carafe it makes a huge mess. A pot of coffee is done in about 6 minutes which is nice. No waiting for 10-12 minutes. The coffee itself is, well a cup of coffee. I didn’t notice a huge difference from my Bunn, and I even ventured out and bought some fine ground Genevalia. The coffee is good and hot, which is where you can tell a significant difference from a Bunn. My Bunn temped at 165 and this one temps at 200 after a cycle completed. The thermos carafe does keep it warm, but not for an extended amount of time. Maybe an hour tops, but make sure you get the lid to the carafe on immediately when it’s done or a lot of heat is lost quickly. Now for my very least favorite thing about this maker. It states it’s a 8 cup coffee maker, which is true. BUT, one very grave point I breezed by in my research is the 8 cups is actually 8 5oz cups. Very few people I know, including myself, drink out of a 5oz coffee cup. Most coffee mugs are 10oz mugs, which means you get 4 regular sized cups of coffee from one carafe. This isn’t ideal when you’re jetting around getting ready for work and have to stop to make another pot.
To sum this up, I’m disappointed with this purchase and had I not have thrown the box away when I got it, I’d send it back and buy another Bunn.
